𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Upon arrival at the scene, the EMS crew found the patient seated on the roadside, conscious and alert. Initial assessment revealed multiple abrasions on both knees and localized swelling extending from the left shoulder to the neck, with no active major bleeding or obvious deformities observed. The patient was safely assisted in walking to the ambulance for further evaluation and monitoring.
First aid was provided by applying povidone-iodine (Betadine) to the affected areas to help prevent infection.
The patient, accompanied by her guardian, was transported via BFP Ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center for further medical evaluation and treatment.
Upon arrival at the hospital, the patient was properly endorsed to the medical staff on duty.

newsArticles.summary:
More than a competition, the SAKURA Challenge, initiated and conducted by Titay Municipal Fire Station, brought together high school students on October 24, 2026, as part of the Naragsakan Festival 2026, to develop lifesaving skills, teamwork, critical thinking, and emergency preparedness through a medical emergency response competition.

Inspired by the beauty of the Sakura flower and the courage of Cardcaptor Sakura, SAKURA (Student Association of Kinship, United Rescuers and Advocates) embodies the belief that even young people can bring hope and make a difference in saving lives. Through this initiative, students are empowered to become capable responders, compassionate helpers, and advocates for a safer and more disaster-resilient community.

Our heartfelt gratitude goes to LGU Titay headed by Mayor Riorita M Castillo, all participating schools, coaches, judges, partners, and supporters who helped make this meaningful event a success. Together, we are nurturing a generation ready to respond, care, and save lives.

newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 
𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel responded to a reported vehicular accident involving a car and a stationary motorcycle in Barangay Namnama, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The responding team immediately proceeded to the scene to ensure scene safety, assess the condition of the involved individuals, and provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.
      Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team ensured scene safety and secured the area before approaching the patient. One (1) female patient was found seated at the roadside, conscious but confused, with a patent airway and spontaneous respirations. Initial assessment revealed a laceration on the forehead, swelling over the left zygomatic and right frontal regions, and an abrasion on the left knee. The patient also complained of dizziness and headache. A laceration of the lower gingiva was noted, reportedly associated with loose dentures.
      Immediate first aid was rendered by applying direct pressure to the lacerations using sterile gauze to control bleeding. The affected wounds were cleansed with an appropriate irrigating solution and covered with sterile gauze dressings. Cold compresses were applied to the areas of swelling to help minimize edema and discomfort. The patient was continuously monitored for changes in level of consciousness, neurological status, and other signs of clinical deterioration.
      The patient was immediately transported via BFP Ambulance to RHU Titay, Poblacion, Zamboanga Sibugay, for definitive management.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A personnel responded to a reported vehicular accident involving a car and a stationary motorcycle in Barangay Palomoc, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The responding team immediately proceeded to the scene to ensure scene safety, assess the condition of the involved individuals, and provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.
Upon arrival at the scene, the responding EMS team ensured scene safety and secured the area before approaching the patients. One (1) male patient was found seated at the roadside, conscious and oriented, with a patent airway and spontaneous respirations. One (1) female patient was also found seated on a chair, conscious and oriented. Initial assessment revealed a puncture wound on the male patient’s left tibial area, an abrasion on the left thigh, and pain in the left shoulder. The female patient was noted to have swelling of the left elbow. 
Immediate first aid was rendered to the male patient by applying direct pressure to the puncture wound using sterile gauze to help control bleeding. The affected wounds were then cleansed with an appropriate irrigating solution and covered with sterile gauze dressings. For the female patient, an arm sling was applied to support and immobilize the affected arm, minimizing unnecessary movement and discomfort. 
Both patients were transported via BFP ambulance to Sibud Hospital in Poblacion, Zamboanga Sibugay, for further medical evaluation, treatment, and definitive management.

A Magnitude 2.3 earthquake was recorded by PHIVOLCS today, 26 June 2026, at 7:09 PM, with its epicenter located 18 km North 22° West of Sarangani Island, Davao Occidental, at a depth of 81 km.

At this magnitude, no damage and aftershocks are expected.

Although this was a minor earthquake, it serves as a reminder that our municipality should always be prepared for any emergency.

🔹 Safety Reminders:
✅ Stay calm and avoid spreading unverified information.
✅ Familiarize yourself with safe evacuation areas and emergency exits.
✅ Prepare and maintain your emergency go bag.
✅ During strong earthquakes, remember: DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.
✅ Follow only official updates from PHIVOLCS and LDRRMO-Titay.

Let us remain vigilant and always practice disaster preparedness. Being prepared today can save lives tomorrow.
